about: Planted bugs. Each one breaks one rule, and the named check must catch it. Spec bugs edit spec/FuzzyMatch.tla and run TLC on the named config: alone, with only the expected invariant, it must be violated, and with the full config, something must be. Oracle bugs edit a copy of tests/tla/drivers/fuzzy_match/oracle.ts or lib.ts, and the oracle stage must report a disagreement with TLC. Code bugs edit a copy of src/core/shared/fuzzy_match.zig, rebuild the harness from it, and the engine stages must report it. Each find string must occur exactly once in its file.

The last word decides the tier instead of the worst.

code.breaks: The run length bound counts the word's punctuation, so a short field misses a run.
Every word skips the text fields, as only the whole query may.
A filter never raises its floor, so near-misses sit beside as-typed hits.
A filter has no fallback, so it goes empty while something matches.
A ranking lists a higher field before a lower one on the same tier.
The ranking iterator walks the worst tier first.
A query longer than the limit still matches by words and letters.
The limit counts one character too many.
The whole-query pass skips a field exactly as long as the query, so a name equal to a long query is missed.
